## Tech Stack

- **Python 3 (stdlib only)** — `operational-indexer.py` uses `json`, `os`, `datetime`, `collections`, `argparse`; no pip dependencies
- **Bash** — `.claude/hooks/cortex-session-start.sh` staleness anchor block
- **JSONL** — `.cortex/edit-ledger.jsonl`; one JSON object per line; matches `facts.jsonl` established pattern

## Conventions

- **Exit 0 always:** Hook scripts never block tool execution. All errors are soft-fails with warning logs.
- **JSONL pattern:** Append-only writes to `.cortex/*.jsonl`; no in-memory-only state; disk is truth.
- **Async hooks:** PostToolUse entries in `.claude/settings.json` use `async: true` to avoid adding latency.
- **Per-skill inline reads:** Operational context is delivered via per-skill SKILL.md read steps, not via additionalContext (budget constraint: 1,604-char worst-case headroom).
- **Soft-fail everywhere:** All operational layer reads in skills must soft-fail silently if `.cortex/edit-ledger.jsonl` is absent or corrupt.
- **No mode-gating:** Unlike `dirty-files.json` (execute/repair only), the operational ledger captures all modes.

## Architecture Rules

- PostToolUse is the capture event; `session_id` from the payload is the co-change grouping key.
- The operational layer is additive — it does not modify, replace, or gate the structural or distilled layers.
- Hook is registered alongside `structural-indexer.py` in `.claude/settings.json` (separate async entries).
- The ledger caps at 500 entries; pruning happens at append time (not read time).
- `/clear` fragments `session_id` — treat co-change signal as approximate, not authoritative.

## Write Boundaries

- `scripts/cortex/operational-indexer.py` — new file
- `.cortex/edit-ledger.jsonl` — new file, created on first hook fire
- `.claude/settings.json` — additive PostToolUse entry only
- `~/.claude/skills/cortex-clarify/SKILL.md` — additive step only (Phase 2d)
- `~/.claude/skills/cortex-spec/SKILL.md` — additive step only (Phase 1e)
- `.claude/hooks/cortex-session-start.sh` — additive anchor block only
